summary: Same 6-arm pinwheel motif (arms spawn at the outer corners and sweep inward, white-hot tips, saturated rainbow rays) but the port launches wheels twice as fast, sweeps them inward ~2x too fast, SPINS THE OPPOSITE WAY, replaces the original's 13.1 s loud/quiet breathing cycle with a flat 3.93 s one, and runs ~40% dimmer with full blackouts between wheels.
observations: Motif matches: on both sides the figure is a 6-fold pinwheel (angular DFT over r=3..30 px on a 64x64 render shows k=6 dominant with mag 0.4-0.85 and k=12 as its harmonic, on every one of 53 frames sampled across 13 s). Arm count is 6 on both, at every phase of both cycles.

Mechanism matches: the brightness-weighted radial centroid (normalised so the grid half-width = 1.0) shows arms appearing at r ~1.2-1.4 (the corners, outside the inscribed circle) and travelling INWARD toward r~0 on BOTH sides. Confirmed on the default 16x16 rig as well as 64x64.

LAUNCH CADENCE 2x TOO FAST. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness (30-180 s windows) gives orig a base period of 0.80 s and port 0.40 s. Identical numbers at 10, 20 and 40 fps (orig 8f/16f/32f; port 4f/8f/15f), so this is a real time-base error, not frame coupling.

INWARD SWEEP ~2x TOO FAST. Radial centroid at 64x64/100 fps: orig falls 1.259 -> 0.569 over 0.33 s (-2.1 half-widths/s); port falls 1.218 -> 0.204 over 0.26 s (-3.9 half-widths/s). On the default 16x16 rig the same measurement gives orig ~-1.1 and port ~-3.8 half-widths/s. Consequence: the port's wheel reaches the centre and dies before the next one launches, while the original's generations overlap.

ROTATION DIRECTION IS REVERSED. Two independent methods agree. (a) Unwrapped phase of the k=6 angular harmonic: orig drifts NEGATIVE everywhere measured (-14.5 deg/frame at 100 fps and -36.4 deg/frame at 40 fps in the decay phase = -242 deg/s physical both times; -95 deg/frame at 100 fps during a buildup near t=7.3 s), port drifts POSITIVE everywhere (+9.0 deg/frame at 100 fps and +23 deg/frame at 40 fps in decay = +150 deg/s physical both times; +95..+150 deg/frame near t=7.1 s). (b) Angular-profile cross-correlation restricted to +/-29 deg (inside the 60 deg ambiguity window a 6-fold figure allows): orig -2.5 to -6 deg/frame, port +2.5 to +7 deg/frame, over the 100 fps bright phases. Confirmed on the default 16x16 rig too (orig k6 phase 137->104->83->55->13->-37; port 9->20->42->58->90->105). Checked in 4+ well-separated time windows per side, always the same sign.

LONG CYCLE IS WRONG AND FLAT. Autocorrelation over 180 s at 20 fps: the original has an extremely strong super-cycle at 262 frames = 13.10 s (r=0.98, recurring at 524/786/1048 frames) with sidebands at +/-16 frames (its 0.80 s base pulse). The port's equivalent peak is at 79 frames = 3.93 s (r=0.89) with +/-8-frame sidebands. Both fps-invariant (orig 13.10 s at 10/20 fps; port 3.92-3.95 s at 10/20/40 fps). 3.93 s is not 13.10/2 = 6.55 s, so it is not explained by the 2x base-rate error.

The original visibly BREATHES over that 13.1 s cycle and the port does not: 5-second-bin mean brightness over 180 s swings 1.8 -> 7.3 on the original (quiet stretches where the rig is nearly dark alternating with loud stretches) but only 2.4 -> 3.4 on the port. The original's rhythm image shows chevron/V-shaped bright bands; the port's is uniform horizontal banding.

PORT IS DIMMER AND SPARSER. Whole-rig mean brightness over 180 s: orig 4.53, port 2.90 (64%). Over a phase-matched sample (120 frames spread across 38.95 s = exactly 3 original super-cycles and 10 port super-cycles): mean brightness orig 4.46 vs port 2.54 (57%); fraction of pixels lit above 10/255 orig 12.66% vs port 6.75%. Peak per-frame mean brightness orig 19 vs port 14.

PORT BLACKS OUT EVERY CYCLE. Frames with meanBrightness exactly 0 over 180 s: orig 6.3%, port 13.8%; meanBrightness <= 1: orig 26.1%, port 41.9%. On the default rig at 40 fps the port's total lit energy collapses to 2-12 (essentially nothing) for ~0.06-0.08 s of every 0.40 s cycle, e.g. t=0.425-0.475 and t=0.825-0.875; the original's minimum between launches is ~160 (a visible decaying tail).

PALETTE FAMILY MATCHES, DISTRIBUTION IS SKEWED. Mean HSV saturation of lit pixels is 0.870 (orig) vs 0.869 (port) and both have white-hot 255 cores, so the colour character is right. But over the phase-matched 38.95 s sample the hue histogram differs: port puts 33.9% of lit pixels in hue 0-60 deg (red/orange) vs the original's 20.4%, and only 21.4% in 180-270 deg (cyan/blue) vs the original's 35.7%. Both sides are green-poor (120-180 deg under 5%).

Both sides are RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT in the same way: rendering at 16x16 and 48x48 gives identical stats (orig mean 7 motion 10 at both; port mean 3 motion 5 at both), i.e. both draw into a fixed logical canvas rather than rasterising at native resolution.
Neither side is frame-rate coupled: at 10/20/40 fps the mean brightness is orig 4.67/4.71/4.74 and port 2.89/2.96/2.94, and every autocorrelation period converts to the same number of SECONDS.

Neither side is seed-driven: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce byte-identical summary stats on both sides (orig mean 5 motion 8, port mean 3 motion 5 over 20 s), so the pattern is fully deterministic and no per-seed randomness caveat applies.
Both sides render cleanly - no compile or runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both, so the synthetic sensor feed is not involved.
feedback: Halve the port's overall time base. The wheel-launch cadence is 0.40 s where the original's is 0.80 s (measured by autocorrelation of mean brightness at 10, 20 and 40 fps - all agree), and the inward sweep runs at ~-3.9 half-widths/s where the original does ~-2.1. Both errors are almost exactly 2x, so one shared speed factor is likely the culprit.

Reverse the spin. The port's pinwheel rotates in the opposite angular direction from the original's, consistently, in every window measured and on both the default 16x16 rig and 48x48/64x64 overrides. Original: k=6 harmonic phase decreases with time (about -242 deg/s of physical rotation during the decay phase). Port: it increases (about +150 deg/s in the same phase). This is almost certainly a sign flip on the angular/time term, or a mirrored y (or x) axis.

The original's arms overlap between launches; the port's do not. Because the port's wheel sweeps all the way to r~0.1 and fades before the next launch, the rig goes COMPLETELY dark for roughly 15-20% of every 0.40 s cycle (13.8% of frames are exactly zero over 180 s vs 6.3% on the original). Slowing the sweep (previous item) plus a longer decay tail on the fading rays should restore the original's continuous glow - the original's residual lit energy never drops below ~5% of its peak between wheels.

Restore the long modulation. The original has a very strong 13.10 s super-cycle (autocorrelation r=0.98) that makes the whole pattern breathe - 5 s-bin mean brightness swings from 1.8 to 7.3, i.e. quiet near-dark stretches alternating with dense bright stretches. The port has a 3.93 s super-cycle instead and its 5 s-bin brightness is flat (2.4-3.4): to a viewer the port has no breathing at all. Note 3.93 s is NOT 13.10/2, so fixing the 2x base-rate error alone will not produce it; the slow modulator's period looks independently wrong (roughly 3.3x too fast).

Raise overall output. Over a phase-matched 38.95 s window (3 full original cycles / 10 full port cycles) the port's mean brightness is 2.54 vs the original's 4.46 and it lights 6.75% of pixels vs 12.66%. Peak frames are 14 vs 19. Some of this will come back with the slower sweep (more overlap), but the port's per-frame peak energy is also lower - the original's loudest frames reach total lit energy ~48000 at 64x64 vs the port's ~31000.

Rebalance the palette walk. Saturation and the white-hot core are already right (mean sat 0.870 vs 0.869 on both), but the port spends too long in red/orange and too little in cyan/blue: 33.9% of lit pixels in hue 0-60 deg vs the original's 20.4%, and 21.4% in 180-270 deg vs the original's 35.7%. Both are correctly green-poor. Measure over a whole super-cycle when checking this - a short window is dominated by whatever hue phase it lands in.

Things the port already gets right and should not be broken by a fix: 6 arms (angular DFT k=6 dominant on both at every sampled phase), arms spawning at the corners and moving inward, resolution independence (identical output at 16x16 and 48x48), fps invariance (identical seconds-periods at 10/20/40 fps), determinism across seeds, and an empty control surface matching the original's.
